source.author: verg
source.text: nam neque tum stellis acies obtunsa videtur, nec fratris radiis obnoxia surgere Luna, tenuia nec lanae per caelum vellera ferri; non tepidum ad solem pinnas in litore pandunt dilectae Thetidi alcyones, non ore solutos immundi meminere sues iactare maniplos.
source.text_original: nam neque tum stellis acies obtunsa videtur, / nec fratris radiis obnoxia surgere Luna, / tenuia nec lanae per caelum vellera ferri; / non tepidum ad solem pinnas in litore pandunt / dilectae Thetidi alcyones, non ore solutos / immundi meminere sues iactare maniplos.
source.text_english: For then the stars do not seem to have blunted outlines, nor does the Moon rise subject to her brother’s rays; nor are thin fleeces of wool seen to be borne through the sky. The beloved alcyones of Thetis do not spread their wings on the shore toward the warm sun, nor do filthy pigs remember to toss with their snout the loosened sheaves.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Ab ea enim semper orbis parte completur et fulget, a qua soli vicinior est, nec umbra terrae obscuratur: quod et poeta uno versiculo demonstravit: Nec fratris radiis obnoxia surgere luna.
reuse.text_original: Ab ea enim semper orbis parte completur et fulget, a qua soli vicinior est, nec umbra terrae obscuratur: quod et poeta uno versiculo demonstravit: Nec fratris radiis obnoxia surgere luna.
reuse.text_english: For it is always filled and shines from that part of the world to which it is closest, and is not darkened by the earth’s shadow: this too the poet showed in a single verse: Nor is the moon subject to rising beneath her brother’s rays.
